title: Grid Paths
statement:
A robot stands at the top-left cell of a grid and wants to reach the bottom-right cell. In `grid`, `0` means a free cell and `1` means a blocked cell. The robot may only move **one cell right or one cell down** at a time, and never enters a blocked cell.

Return the **number of different paths** from the top-left to the bottom-right cell. If either of those two cells is blocked, the answer is `0`.
constraints: 1 <= rows, cols <= 12 (every row has the same length)

examples.explanation: Go around the blocked centre cell, either above or below it.
Down then right is the only way.

hints.nudge: To arrive at a cell, the robot must have come from just two possible cells. Which ones?
hints.pattern: Dynamic programming on the grid: paths(cell) = paths(above) + paths(left).
hints.walkthrough: Exploring every path with recursion repeats the same sub-paths many times. The number of ways to reach a free cell is the ways to reach the cell above plus the ways to reach the cell to its left, because the robot's last move was either down or right. A blocked cell has 0 ways. Fill the grid row by row starting with the start cell set to 1 (or 0 if it is blocked); the bottom-right value is the answer. O(rows * cols) time. The biggest possible answer (12x12, nothing blocked) is 705,432, so it fits in an int.
